description: Seed content for the vertical slice in math-tutor-build-plan.md (Phase 1 + 14). Contains the linear-functions skill graph and a problem bank with hand-authored deep-themed variants.
usage_notes: Each problem has a `neutral` realization plus `themed` realizations. PREFER the themed realization matching the student's chosen theme; runtime must display the selected `prompt` exactly. The LLM may respond around it but MUST NOT rewrite, re-narrate, embellish, or change the problem text, numbers, units, roles, or relationships.
Each realization carries its OWN `canonical_answer` because realistic numbers differ across domains. The code checker (domain/checker.py) grades against the realization actually shown to the student.

These authored variants also serve as FEW-SHOT EXEMPLARS for the contextualizer (domain/contextualizer.py) when theming a skill for which no variant is pre-written. They demonstrate DEEP theming: the math genuinely arises from the situation (slope = travel rate / resource use / velocity; intercept = starting value), never a cosmetic rename.

`canonical_answer` uses the variable named in that realization's prompt (x, d, t, k, ...). The checker MUST sympify with: implicit-multiplication enabled, '^' converted to '**', numeric tolerance for decimals, and the prompt's variable symbol.
`solution_method` is private/offline source material. Runtime prompts receive only a derived `hint_scaffold` that excludes final answers and immediate next computed values.

assessment_role: 'practice' (default) or 'transfer' is a candidate marker only. transfer_passed is computed by the scheduler relative to the student's contexts_seen, prior RealizedProblemRefs, representation history, and theme history; the static content tag is not sufficient by itself. Retention is timing-based and reuses any item, so no special content is needed.

themes.label: Space colony logistics
themes.mapping_hint: Slope = a rate (km traveled per day, litres used per hour, crates delivered per day). y-intercept = a starting stock or starting position. Negative slope = something being consumed.

themes.label: Drone / flight motion
themes.mapping_hint: Linear (not quadratic) aspects only: horizontal position vs time (slope = constant horizontal velocity); vertical velocity vs time (slope = -g ~ -10, a genuinely deep link); steady climb/descent. Do NOT theme linear skills onto height-vs-time, which is parabolic.

skills.name: Read and write coordinates
skills.description: Locate and name points (x, y) on the coordinate plane.

skills.name: Rate of change as constant slope
skills.description: Recognise a constant rate of change from a table or situation.

skills.name: Slope from a graph
skills.description: Read slope as rise over run from a graphed line.

skills.name: Identify the y-intercept
skills.description: Identify the starting value / where the line meets the vertical axis.

skills.name: Write y = mx + b
skills.description: Construct the equation of a line from slope and intercept, two points, or context.

skills.name: Evaluate / solve a linear model

skills.name: Interpret slope and intercept in context
skills.description: Explain what the slope and intercept mean for the real situation.

neutral.prompt: A point is 4 units to the right of the origin and 3 units up. Write its coordinates as (x, y).
neutral.solution_method: Right is the +x direction and up is the +y direction, so the point is (4, 3).

space_logistics.prompt: On a colony map the origin is your base station. A research station lies 4 km east and 3 km north. Give its map coordinates (east, north) in km.
space_logistics.solution_method: East acts as +x, north as +y, so the station is at (4, 3).

drone_physics.prompt: On a survey chart the sensor sits at the origin. A sensor marker is 4 units to the right (x) and 3 units up (y). Give the coordinates (x, y).
drone_physics.solution_method: Right is +x and up is +y, so the marked point is (4, 3).

hint_scaffold.level_0: Think about the horizontal direction first, then the vertical direction.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Coordinates are written as (x, y): horizontal amount, then vertical amount.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Use the right/east amount for x and the up/north amount for y, without changing their order.

neutral.prompt: A table shows y at x = 0, 1, 2, 3 as 50, 80, 110, 140. What is the constant rate of change of y per unit x?
neutral.solution_method: Each step of 1 in x increases y by 80-50 = 30, and the jumps are equal, so the constant rate is 30.

space_logistics.prompt: A colony depot's water-tank count by day (a cargo route resupplies each night): Day 0 = 50, Day 1 = 80, Day 2 = 110, Day 3 = 140. What is the daily rate of change in tanks?
space_logistics.solution_method: Stock rises by 30 tanks every day (80-50, 110-80, 140-110 are all 30), so the rate is +30 tanks per day.

drone_physics.prompt: A drone climbs steadily. Its altitude in metres at t = 0, 1, 2, 3 seconds is 50, 80, 110, 140. What is the rate of change of altitude per second?
drone_physics.solution_method: Altitude rises 30 m each second (equal jumps), so the rate of climb is 30 m/s.

hint_scaffold.level_0: Look for how the output changes as the input changes.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Rate of change is change in output divided by change in input.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Compare two matching rows, set up output change over input change, and keep the sign from increasing or decreasing output.

neutral.prompt: A table shows y at x = 0, 2, 4, 6 as 200, 170, 140, 110. What is the rate of change of y per unit x?
neutral.solution_method: y falls by 30 each time x rises by 2, so per unit x the rate is -30/2 = -15. (Note x steps by 2, not 1.)

space_logistics.prompt: A rover battery drains during a route survey. Charge remaining vs hours traveled: 0 h = 200, 2 h = 170, 4 h = 140, 6 h = 110. What is the rate of change of charge per hour?
space_logistics.solution_method: Charge drops 30 units every 2 hours, so per hour the rate is -30/2 = -15 units/h. The minus sign means it is being consumed.

drone_physics.prompt: A weather balloon ascending under gravity slows steadily. Its vertical velocity (m/s) is 30 at t = 0, 20 at t = 1, 10 at t = 2, 0 at t = 3 seconds. What is the rate of change of velocity per second?
drone_physics.solution_method: Velocity falls 10 m/s each second, so the rate is -10 m/s per second. That slope is essentially -g, the acceleration of gravity.

hint_scaffold.level_0: Look for how the output changes as the input changes.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Rate of change is change in output divided by change in input.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Compare two matching rows, set up output change over input change, and keep the sign from increasing or decreasing output.

space_logistics.prompt: Two route logs from a steady rover trip: at hour 1 the rover was 4 km past the habitat, at hour 5 it was 16 km past. What is the travel rate (the slope) in km/h?

drone_physics.prompt: A drone moves at constant horizontal speed. Its horizontal position is 4 m at t = 1 s and 16 m at t = 5 s. Find its horizontal speed (the slope).

neutral.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (0, 90) and (6, 30).

space_logistics.prompt: During a rover trip a vehicle's fuel (litres) is 90 at hour 0 and 30 at hour 6. What is the rate of change of fuel per hour?
space_logistics.solution_method: rate = (30 - 90)/(6 - 0) = -60/6 = -10 L/h; negative because fuel is being used.

drone_physics.prompt: A drone's upward velocity is 90 m/s at t = 0 and 30 m/s at t = 6 s. Find the slope (its acceleration).

hint_scaffold.level_0: Use the two points to compare vertical change with horizontal change.

space_logistics.prompt: On a supply chart, the 'crates delivered' line rises 2 crates for every 1 day moved to the right. What is its slope?

drone_physics.prompt: On an altitude-time graph, a climbing drone's altitude line goes up 2 m for every 1 s to the right. What is its slope?

hint_scaffold.level_0: Find the rise and the run from the graph description.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Slope is rise divided by run.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Write the vertical change over the horizontal change, keeping the exact fraction if it is not whole.

neutral.prompt: A line passes through grid points, going up 3 squares for every 4 squares to the right. What is its slope? Give an exact value.

space_logistics.prompt: A 'distance traveled vs fuel used' chart climbs 3 km for every 4 litres used. What is the slope, in km per litre? Give an exact value.
space_logistics.solution_method: slope = rise/run = 3 km / 4 L = 3/4 km per litre.

drone_physics.prompt: A service ramp's profile rises 3 m for every 4 m measured horizontally. What is the slope of the ramp? Give an exact value.

hint_scaffold.level_0: Find the rise and the run from the graph description.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Slope is rise divided by run.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Write the vertical change over the horizontal change, keeping the exact fraction if it is not whole.

neutral.prompt: What is the y-intercept of y = 4x + 7?
neutral.solution_method: In y = mx + b, the y-intercept is b. Here b = 7.

space_logistics.prompt: A depot model is S = 4d + 7, where S is supplies and d is days. How many supplies are there at the start (d = 0)?
space_logistics.solution_method: At d = 0, S = 4(0) + 7 = 7. The starting value is the intercept, 7.

drone_physics.prompt: A horizontal-position model is x = 4t + 7 (t in seconds). What is the starting position at t = 0?
drone_physics.solution_method: At t = 0, x = 4(0) + 7 = 7. The intercept gives the start position, 7.

hint_scaffold.level_0: The intercept is the starting value on the vertical axis.
hint_scaffold.level_1: For an equation in slope-intercept form, look for the constant term.
hint_scaffold.level_2: For a graph or context, identify the value when the input is zero.

neutral.prompt: A line crosses the vertical axis at the point (0, 12). What is its y-intercept?
neutral.solution_method: The y-intercept is the y-value where x = 0, so it is 12.

space_logistics.prompt: A fuel graph meets the vertical axis at (0, 12): the tank held 12 (hundred litres) before the trip began. State the y-intercept.
space_logistics.solution_method: At the start (x = 0, day 0) the value is 12, so the y-intercept is 12.

drone_physics.prompt: An altitude-time graph crosses the vertical axis at (0, 12): the platform sits 12 m above the valley floor. State the y-intercept.
drone_physics.solution_method: At t = 0 the altitude is 12 m, so the y-intercept is 12.

hint_scaffold.level_1: For an equation in slope-intercept form, look for the constant term.

neutral.prompt: Write the equation of a line with slope 5 and y-intercept 20 in the form y = mx + b.
neutral.solution_method: Substitute m = 5 and b = 20 into y = mx + b to get y = 5x + 20.

space_logistics.prompt: A depot starts with 20 crates and receives 5 crates per day. Write supplies S as a function of days d, in the form S = m*d + b.
space_logistics.solution_method: Rate m = 5 (crates/day), start b = 20, so S = 5d + 20.

drone_physics.prompt: A drone begins at 20 m altitude and climbs 5 m each second. Write altitude A as a function of time t, in the form A = m*t + b.
drone_physics.solution_method: Rate m = 5 (m/s), start b = 20, so A = 5t + 20.

hint_scaffold.level_0: An equation in this form combines a rate and a starting value.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Use the pattern output = rate times input plus starting value.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Identify the slope and intercept first, then place them into the slope-intercept form without evaluating a final answer in the hint.

neutral.prompt: A line passes through (0, 6) and (3, 18). Write its equation as y = mx + b.
neutral.solution_method: slope = (18 - 6)/(3 - 0) = 12/3 = 4; the point (0, 6) gives b = 6, so y = 4x + 6.

space_logistics.prompt: At day 0 a depot has 6 (hundred panels); by day 3 it has 18 (hundred), under steady resupply. Write panels P as P = m*d + b.

drone_physics.prompt: A balloon is at 6 m at t = 0 and 18 m at t = 3 s, rising steadily. Write height H as H = m*t + b.

hint_scaffold.level_0: An equation in this form combines a rate and a starting value.
hint_scaffold.level_1: Use the pattern output = rate times input plus starting value.
hint_scaffold.level_2: Identify the slope and intercept first, then place them into the slope-intercept form without evaluating a final answer in the hint.

neutral.prompt: A line has slope -8 and passes through (2, 50). Write its equation as y = mx + b.

space_logistics.prompt: A rover uses 8 litres per km. After 2 km it has 50 litres left. Write fuel F as a function of distance k, in the form F = m*k + b.
space_logistics.solution_method: m = -8 (L/km); b = 50 - (-8)(2) = 66, so F = -8k + 66 (it started with 66 L).

drone_physics.prompt: A training drone reduces its speed by 8 m/s each second. At t = 2 s its speed is 50 m/s. Write speed v as a function of t, in the form v = m*t + b.
drone_physics.solution_method: m = -8 (m/s per s); b = 50 - (-8)(2) = 66, so v = -8t + 66 (initial speed 66 m/s).

problems.grading_note: is_correct is graded ONLY on the signed number below. The qualitative meaning is drawn out by the tutor using `interpretation_rubric` but does NOT flip is_correct (code owns truth; prose is not code-checkable in v1).

neutral.prompt: A quantity is modelled by y = -25x + 300. By how much does y change each time x increases by 1? Give a signed number.
neutral.solution_method: The slope is the change in y per unit x. Here it is -25, so y falls by 25 for each increase of 1 in x.
neutral.interpretation_rubric: Slope -25 = decreasing by 25 per unit. Intercept 300 = the starting value at x = 0. A negative slope means the quantity is shrinking.

space_logistics.prompt: Fuel follows F = -25d + 300 (litres vs days). By how much does fuel change each day? Give a signed number.
space_logistics.solution_method: The slope -25 is the daily change: fuel drops 25 L per day.
space_logistics.interpretation_rubric: Slope -25 = losing 25 L/day. Intercept 300 = the rover started with 300 L. Negative slope = consumption.

drone_physics.prompt: Vertical velocity follows v = -10t + 30 (m/s). By how much does v change each second? Give a signed number.
drone_physics.solution_method: The slope -10 is the change per second: velocity drops 10 m/s each second.
drone_physics.interpretation_rubric: Slope -10 = -g, gravity slowing the upward motion. Intercept 30 = initial speed. The object decelerates, stops, then falls.

hint_scaffold.level_0: Connect the sign and size of the rate to the situation.
hint_scaffold.level_1: The coefficient of the input tells the signed change per one unit of input.
hint_scaffold.level_2: State the signed rate only; the tutor can discuss the meaning after your numeric answer.
